messages:
raj: Quick Q — I want to float a design for Private BYOK: run a local sidecar KMS-proxy that forwards API calls to the customer's HSM/KMS. How do we lock down RBAC and audit so we never leak key material or sensitive key identifiers in our logs? (thinking SOC2 / PCI auditors will ask for chain-of-custody details)
emma: High level: 1) minimal IAM for the proxy (only Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign where needed), 2) never log raw key IDs — store only a one-way fingerprint, 3) ensure trace-id propagation so customer logs and our audit events can be correlated.
maria: For compliance: we need verifiable events at the boundary. Each proxied operation should emit an audit record containing: timestamp, requestor identity (role), operation, hashed_key_fingerprint, trace_id, and a nonce. That lets auditors map request -> HSM event without exposing the customer's key material.
raj: Example audit payload (pseudocode):
```json
{
  "ts": "2026-02-10T15:12:34Z",
  "actor": "service-account:payment-ingest",
  "operation": "Decrypt",
  "key_fingerprint": "sha256:3d2f...",
  "trace_id": "rwd-abc123",
  "outcome": "success",
  "proxy_version": "v0.6.1"
}
```
Note: key_fingerprint must be one-way (no reversible mapping stored by Redwood).
ops-bot: Heads-up: when we roll the sidecar, add a middleware stage to scrub env vars and redact any header that looks like `x-key-id` or matches `/key(_?id)?/i`. Also add a configurable redact-list for customer-specific header patterns.
adele: On the vuln side: there's an advisory for a PKCS#11 wrapper we use (CVE-2025-1234). We should: 1) determine if the sidecar links that lib, 2) plan a backport/patch, 3) add seccomp/sandboxing around the sidecar process, 4) prepare a communication template for affected customers. If the HSM vendor has attestation APIs, prefer those over parsing raw PKCS11 responses.
maria: Incident playbook sketch (short):
1) Confirm exploit or anomalous call pattern against proxy metrics
2) Quarantine sidecar fleet (disable outbound to customer KMS)
3) Pull HSM audit logs from customer side (using provided log pull process) and our proxy audit stream (hashed fingerprints + traces)
4) Notify customers + compliance (SOC2 contact) with timeline and CVE references
5) Rotate any wrapping/wrappable keys (non-exportable wrappers) if compromise suspected
6) Post-incident: provide signed attestation that we executed the rotation + preserved chain-of-custody artifacts
emma: RBAC proposal (minimal):
- role: kms-proxy-invoker (allowed: kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:Sign)
- role: kms-proxy-admin (allowed: kms:CreateAlias, kms:Rotate, kms:Disable)
Policy snippets: `"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": "arn:...:key/*:fingerprint-<hashed>"` 
Ensure the policy never includes kms:ExportKey or equivalent.
raj: Nice. Action items: emma to draft the formal IAM policy + example least-privilege YAML, adele to confirm PKCS#11 patch status and mitigation timeline, ops to add redact middleware and tests. I can draft the audit schema and a minimal compliance FAQ for SOC2/PCI.
maria: Also add a retention note: keep proxy audit stream for 1 year by default for enterprise customers (configurable), and ensure we can provide sliced exports with trace_id filtering.
ops-bot: CI checklist: unit test for redaction, integration test that fingerprinting is deterministic but non-reversible, load test to ensure sidecar doesn't add >10ms p95 latency for common paths.
emma: I'll put a PR up tomorrow with the policy and a basic runbook page.
raj: Thanks — marking this thread for follow-up in the security sprint. :white_check_mark:
